text:
mira (vp-product): quick follow-up from todays all-hands Q&A — folks asked for a single narrative we can use externally plus clear guidance for product tradeoffs. can leadership confirm? cc @alex

alex (ceo): short answer: mission unchanged  make inference predictable, economical, and portable. we need one-line exec pitch + a slightly nerdy SE variant + a tiny prioritization rubric for PMs/eng.

anika (marketing): can we get an exec-friendly header (1 line) and a ~20-word technical blurb? marketing will A/B test.

alex (ceo): draft exec: "Redwood: production-first inference — a single API for fast dev velocity and predictable performance across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."

anika (marketing): nice. SE blurb suggestion?

lee (cto): SE blurb: "High-throughput runtime with workload-aware batching and KV prefix caching, plus policy-based routing for predictable cost/latency tradeoffs." keep it short.

taylor (sales): useful. sales also needs sequencing guidance: lead with Hosted or lead with Dedicated for mid-market pursuits?

alex (ceo): recommended sequence: start with Hosted trials for velocity. escalate to Dedicated when customers need guaranteed latency/isolation. Private is for compliance-only scenarios. use "trial -> reserved commit" as the playbook.

mira (vp-product): PMs asked about prioritization signal: when should kernel/runtime perf outrank admin UX?

lee (cto): propose a pragmatic rule: any anonymized deal > $Y ARR requiring p50 < 60ms gets expedited perf work. otherwise admin/ops improvements remain high ROI.

alex (ceo): agreed. product to publish the anonymized prioritized deals list + SLO guideline so eng can plan sprints.

ops-bot: created task P-8009 in #product-ops: "Publish one-liner, SE blurb, SLO rubric, and sales sequencing playbook" assigned to @mira and @anika, due in 4 business days.

anika (marketing): will draft two microcopy variants and the one-pager, post in #marketing for feedback.

taylor (sales): also request a short objection-handling line vs vendors that only do model access or only on-prem. buyers tend to compare checklists.

alex (ceo): suggested objection line: "Unlike providers focused solely on model access or only on on-prem hardware, Redwood pairs a production-grade runtime with deployment flexibility and measurable unit economics." keep it non-branded.

mira (vp-product): perfect. i'll assemble the drafts and the prioritized-deals doc and link them here when ready. if anyone has exceptions to the prioritization rule, DM me with rationale. :thumbsup:
